verify.name: content-parses
verify.expect: all SIX suites print OK, each naming how much it examined: posts; blockquote fixtures + corpus blockquotes; sanitize cases + corpus html nodes + embed blocks; smartypants cases + corpus text nodes + inline-code nodes; island-guard blog slug cases (incl. a cross-collection subset) + corpus slugs + PAGE slug cases (incl. a cross-collection subset) + corpus page slugs + control-character cases + .mdx documents inventoried + settings-path cases + island-name cases + icon-name cases; and page prose bodies + words + pages + blocks + empty rich-text fields skipped, all asserted to parse without an invalid_markdown node, with Vale's own file count reconciled against them. Treat the numbers as floors that grow when fixtures are added — but a suite that stops naming one of those categories has lost coverage, which is the failure this line exists to catch.
verify.why: Aggregates check:content, check:blockquotes, check:sanitize, check:smartypants, check:island-guard and check:page-prose. Each asserts it ran over a non-empty corpus — a Tina collection, a Vale glob and an embed counter have all reported success over nothing on this branch. check:page-prose exists because a `.vale.ini` section pointed at content/pages/**/*.mdx reports '0 errors in 2 files' and KEEPS reporting it with banned words in the prose: the bodies live in YAML frontmatter, which Vale does not read. It extracts them, lints them as real files, and fails if Vale's trailing 'in N files' count does not equal the number it wrote — which is what catches the .vale.ini section being removed. The island-guard control-character cases exist to kill an `m` flag on the slug patterns: under /m the `$` anchors to a LINE end, so `about\n../settings/index` would validate while every other fixture still passed.

verify.name: tina-indexes-posts
verify.expect: OK: Tina indexes blog=17 settings=1 page=2
verify.why: `tinacms audit` prints '✅ Audit passed' and exits 0 on an EMPTY collection, so the counts must be asserted explicitly. A wrong collection path/format/glob would otherwise build all 59 pages with no posts, exit 0, and deploy. Asserts per-collection since Task 2.1: the script fails if a named collection is missing from the audit, if a count is wrong, AND if the audit reports a collection nobody asserted. That third mode did its job in Task 3.1 — the `page` collection failed this gate with 'audit reported the page collection but no expected count was given' until `page=2` was added here. `page=2` is home.mdx + about.mdx; a page added in the CMS must be added to this count, and until Task 3.2 lands the catch-all route that is the ONLY gate that notices a page document at all.

verify.name: build-and-routes
verify.command: bun run build:local && find dist/client -name '*.html' | sed 's|^dist/client||' | sort | diff .baseline/routes.txt -
verify.expect: only difference is an added /admin/index.html (the TinaCMS admin SPA); all 59 site routes present
verify.why: `bun run build` alone fails without a Tina server — use build:local. Output moved to dist/client + dist/server when the Cloudflare adapter landed, so the route diff must target dist/client. Tina's datalayer binds 9000 and its client hardcodes localhost:4001; the scripts pin --datalayer-port 9007. Both scripts also set NODE_ENV=production, because `tinacms build` otherwise runs its subcommand with NODE_ENV=development, which folds import.meta.env.DEV to true and compiles postFilter to `return true` — publishing every draft and scheduled post.

verify.name: prose
verify.expect: 0 errors — and check the trailing 'in N files' count is 17, not 0
verify.why: Vale reports success on an empty file set. The .vale.ini glob is extension-scoped, so renaming posts silently pointed it at zero files once already.

verify.name: lint
verify.expect: EXACTLY 3 errors + 1 warning: 'Found 3 errors.' / 'Found 1 warning.' over 93 files. Four diagnostics over three files: the 3 errors are DESIGN.json (format), src/utils/og-templates/post.js (format), src/utils/og-templates/site.js (format); the 1 warning is src/utils/og-templates/post.js:2:8 lint/correctness/noUnusedImports (unused `SITE` import) — so post.js accounts for two of the four, and four diagnostics is NOT four errors. All pre-existing on main. src/components/Header.astro was on this list until Task 2.1, when the settings-prop edit supplied the blank line after its imports that was its only complaint — its absence is a fix, not a regression.
verify.why: Not a clean gate. Any file outside that list is a regression introduced by this branch. READ THE COUNT, AND READ EVERY '━━━' HEADER — DO NOT grep the output for a file-name pattern. Biome prints format diagnostics as 'path format' but lint/assist diagnostics as 'path:line:col rule', so a filter anchored on the filename followed by a space silently hides every assist/organizeImports failure. That is exactly how Task 2.1 reported '3 files, clean' while the gate was actually failing on 4 branch-modified files (src/constants.ts, src/layouts/AboutLayout.astro, src/pages/blog/[...page].astro, src/pages/tags/[tag]/[...page].astro). The 'Found N errors' line never reconciled with the filtered list and that was the tell.
